thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for `az1-inference-overload` (P0) — multiple throttles and timeouts observed, 1xx-5xx spike. page: pd-PRD-az1-0001

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert triggered -> Escalation policy: " + "AZ1 Production Oncall. Notification sent.

oncall-sre: Acked. I'm on it — checking nodes and control-plane.

sre_alex: grabbing logs now. seeing a sudden CPU/GPU eviction pattern on az1-gpu-pool-3, spot reclaim churn.

sre_jules: confirmed — VM eviction count spiked at 14:17 UTC. Pods are being rescheduled but throttled because autoscaler is throttling back.

eng_mike: @oncall-sre if this is due to spot evictions we should flip routing to az2 read-mostly and enable dedicated burst in dedicated pools. Initiating failover plan B.

oncall-sre: Doing incremental steps: 1) scale down batch_size for model v3 to reduce GPU memory pressure, 2) enable prefix cache bypass for hot paths, 3) route 30% traffic to az2. Will update.

sre_alex: Running commands to drain degraded nodes and get pods rescheduled:

```
# cordon and drain one bad node
kubectl cordon gpu-az1-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-az1-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

sre_jules: Patch to autoscaler to be less conservative for scale-up: applying now.

```
kubectl apply -f autoscaler-temporary-bump.yaml
# autoscaler-temporary-bump.yaml reduces cooldowns and increases max replicas
```

ops_manager: Notifying support roster + opening incident in PagerDuty notes. Taking ownership of customer communication.

pm_sahil: Heads-up — two large customers in EU are seeing elevated latencies; statuspage draft in progress. If we need to failover region-wide, I'll coordinate messaging.

statusbot: Status page draft created: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1777778888 (private draft).

eng_mike: I'm starting a targeted model rollback for v3 -> v2 on az1 to reduce VRAM footprint. Rolling canary to 5% first.

oncall-sre: Can you post the rollback command?

eng_mike:```
# rollback canary
redwoodctl rollout set --service inference-v3 --version v2 --region az1 --traffic 5%
```

sre_alex: Metrics snippet (17:12-17:30 UTC):
```
- 95th latency: 3200ms -> 9800ms spike
- 5xx rate: 0.2% -> 12.7% at peak
- evictions/min: 0.1 -> 3.4
```

oncall-sre: Traffic routing update: shifting 30% to az2 via smart-router. Command: `routectl shift --from az1 --to az2 --pct 30` — executing in 2m.

sre_jules: After routing shift, see immediate drop in timeouts from some customer classes. But tail latency still high for long-context requests.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by oncall-sre. Escalation level remains 1.

oncall-sre: Eng Mike — can you reduce default max_tokens for streaming to cut tail? That config is in inference-config.

eng_mike: Done, pushed small config change: `inference-config:set --region az1 --defaults max_tokens=512` — rolling.

ops_manager: Preparing incident bridge in 5m. Dial-in -> https://meet.redwood.example/incident-1777778888

pm_sahil: Customer comms draft ready, will publish after we confirm stabilization window of 15m.

sre_alex: Good news: 5xx rate down to 2.1% post-shift and rollback. 95th latency ~2200ms. Still above SLO but improving.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Reminder — if incident exceeds 45m without recovery escalate to senior-sre.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged. Planning to keep route at 30% until autoscaler finishes cooldown and drained nodes return.

eng_mike: Pushing an emergency patch to inference runtime to bypass expensive attention kernel for long-context requests on az1; patch will take ~8m.

sre_jules: Patch applied, monitoring.

sre_alex: Evictions stopped, node count stable. Autoscaler reports desired replicas +6, available +4. We're getting there.

oncall-sre: Status update for customers: posted to draft, publishing now.

statusbot: Status page updated (public): https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1777778888 — "Partial degradation in az1 affecting inference latency and errors; mitigation in progress."

pm_sahil: Published. Customer-first line posted to main support channels.

ops_manager: Handing off to night oncall in 35 minutes. Current plan: keep az2 routing at 30% until full recovery; rollback model canary to v2 if any regressions.

oncall-sre: Going to start a controlled traffic ramp-down back to az1 when 95th < 1s for 20m.

sre_jules: We're at 95th = 980ms for last 8m. Good trend.

oncall-sre: Handoff: @sre_alex will cover the next shift. I will add notes: actions taken, commands run, metrics.

sre_alex: I have the bridge and logs. Taking over monitoring. Thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident resolved? Not yet. Marking as 'stabilized' when both latency and 5xx meet targets for 30m.

pagerduty: Notification: incident status changed to "stabilizing".

ops_manager: Closing notes will include root cause hypothesis (spot eviction + autoscaler cooldown + recent model rollout) and follow-ups: 1) add eviction-aware placements 2) increase autoscaler headroom, 3) add PD rule to seed extra capacity on eviction storms.

pm_sahil: I'll coordinate customer postmortem and a short outbound.

sre_alex: Last log excerpt (17:45 UTC):
```
[2026-03-14T17:45:12Z] inference-proxy: conn_id=abcd1234 latency=520ms status=200 model=embed-v2
[2026-03-14T17:45:13Z] nodewatch: eviction_count=0
```

sre_jules: Leaving reactions and further details in the incident doc.

oncall-sre: Handing off live monitoring to @sre_alex. I'm going offline for rotation.

sre_alex: Acknowledged. I'll take over and escalate if metrics regress.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: oncall-sre has ACKed and marked handoff to sre_alex.

statusbot: Incident status updated: "stabilizing" -> public update queued.

(thumbsup)"
